headline: A new coding-agent benchmark reports frequent harmful side effects alongside task success
summary: A 2 November 2026 preprint introduces VeriHarm-Bench, a 150-task shell-scripting benchmark that pairs task-correctness tests with executable tests for designated harmful side effects. Across four held-out coding agents, the authors report 95.1% average task accuracy, 58.2% harmful success and 37.0% safe success. A human review of 50 sampled benchmark items found higher majority-vote validity among top-ranked than bottom-ranked items, with moderate annotator agreement. The results are author-reported and apply to this curated benchmark; they do not estimate real-world incident rates or broad coding-agent safety, and no independent reproduction was inspected.
